description: sRGB and Display-P3 to CIE XYZ (D65). The chromaticity entries are the published primaries and white point; the test re-derives the matrix from them and asserts it matches the stored one, so the citation is checked rather than asserted. The primary entries are definitional: the XYZ of primary N is column N of the matrix, which is what makes a transposed matrix impossible to miss.

entries.derivationNote: Each component 0.5 linearises to ((0.5 + 0.055)/1.055)^2.4 = 0.21404114048223255, then XYZ = white x 0.21404114048223255. The Y of 0.2140 is why 50% grey carries 21.4% of the light.

8-bit code 3 on every channel: 3/255 = 0.011764705882352941, linearises to 0.0009105809506465125 on the LINEAR branch, then XYZ = white x that. A pure-power implementation returns roughly a 39th of this Y.

entries.derivationNote: P3 [1,0,0] through the P3 matrix, then the XYZ-to-sRGB matrix, then the OETF. Only the SIGNS are definitional — P3 red must fall outside sRGB — so the entry is classed by how its numbers were obtained, not by the property it demonstrates.
